segments.narration: A telescope heard something once and never again. August 1977, Ohio. Seventy-two seconds of narrow radio noise from Sagittarius.
Jerry Ehman found it on the printout days later. He circled the letters and wrote one word in the margin: Wow.
It sat almost exactly on the hydrogen line, 1420 megahertz. That frequency is protected, and it is where you would listen for someone.
Seventy-two seconds is exactly how long the beam took to sweep that patch of sky, so the source was out there, not on Earth.
Dozens of searches since have found nothing there. A 2017 comet explanation was proposed, and other astronomers took it apart.
